_comment: The artist's own capture rig. Stated by the artist on 2026-09-08. This is a MEASUREMENT of how his footage is shot, not a default for every clip in the workspace: stock and reference plates (reporter_test) carry their own camera block in shot.json and must not inherit these values.

lens.squeeze_factor_status: SIRUI Saturn series specification; CONFIRM against the lens barrel before it is used in a camera solve
lens.sensor_width_note: Full-frame nominal. The recorded sensor width times the squeeze factor gives the effective horizontal field of view; see horizontal_fov_deg.

shutter.exposure_note: 180 degrees at 24 fps is 1/48 s. Blender's motion blur must be set to shutter 0.5 (fraction of the frame interval) for CG elements to carry matching blur; the default 0.5 happens to be correct, but set it explicitly rather than inheriting it.

white_balance.note: Daylight-balanced. An environment lit warmer or cooler than 5600 K will not match the plate's rendering of skin unless the relight ratio carries the difference; do not neutralise the plate to grey and then relight, or the correction is applied twice.

pipeline_implications: ANAMORPHIC SQUEEZE IS THE BIGGEST ONE. The recorded plate is horizontally squeezed by the squeeze factor. Blender renders spherically, so plate and CG do not share a projection until one of them is converted. Decide the working space explicitly per shot and record it: either desqueeze the plate on ingest and render spherical CG at the desqueezed aspect, or keep the plate squeezed and render CG with a matching horizontal scale. Every geometric stage downstream -- camera solve, depth back-projection, normals, proxy geometry -- reads pixel aspect from that decision, and a silent 1.6x error there is exactly the kind of fault that is invisible in one frame.
Depth and normal estimators are trained on spherical imagery. Run them on the DESQUEEZED plate, or a face is 1.6x too narrow and the estimated geometry is wrong in a way that looks plausible.

Defocus is oval, not round: an anamorphic bokeh is stretched vertically by the squeeze factor in the desqueezed image. Blender's circular aperture will not match; the background defocus needs an anisotropic treatment.

Field of view: at 35 mm with a 1.6x squeeze on a 36 mm full-frame sensor, the horizontal coverage is that of a 21.9 mm spherical lens while the vertical stays that of a 35 mm. Do not feed 35 mm to a spherical camera model.
Flares and streaks are horizontal and typically blue. If the environment contains practicals in frame, matching this is part of the photorealism bar, not a stylistic extra.
horizontal_fov_derivation: 2*atan(36 / (2 * 35/1.6)) = 79.0 deg. Equivalent spherical focal length 35/1.6 = 21.9 mm.
vertical_fov_derivation: 2*atan(24 / (2*35)) = 37.8 deg for a full 24 mm sensor height; 27.0 deg is quoted for a 2.39:1 desqueezed extraction. Record the actual recording mode per shot rather than relying on either figure.
still_to_record: Camera body and recording codec / bit depth / colour profile (log or Rec.709).
Recording mode and sensor readout area, which fixes the vertical field of view.
The artist's own interocular distance, measured once with a ruler, to remove the 63 mm adult prior from every camera solve.
A chrome ball and an 18% grey ball on a slate at the head of every take, which converts E_source from an assumption into a measurement.
